description: The left column shows linear structures and the right column nonlinear structures. The hash table appears separately below both columns to illustrate a key-value mapping.

frames.explanation: Linear structures have a sequential order, but differ in where operations can take place. Trees and heaps form parent-child hierarchies, while a graph allows a vertex to have multiple neighbors. These are logical relationships. The underlying storage can vary for the same relationship, and a hash table can combine arrays, linked lists, or trees.
frames.title: Logical relationships in data structures

summary: Compare four logical relationships: sequences, parent-child hierarchies, network connections, and key-value mappings.
